prompt: Base treatment of a mixture of acetaldehyde and propanal gives a mixture of aldol products. How many possible products does the section describe?
explanation: Each aldehyde can be either the enolate donor or the acceptor, giving two "symmetrical" products (3-hydroxybutanal and 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal) and two "mixed" products (3-hydroxy-2-methylbutanal and 3-hydroxypentanal). Such a reaction is of no practical value.

prompt: Which of these is one of the two "mixed" aldol products formed from acetaldehyde and propanal?

choices.why: That is a symmetrical product, formed from two acetaldehyde molecules.
That is a symmetrical product, formed from two propanal molecules.
A mixed product has 2 + 3 = 5 carbons; 3-hydroxyhexanal has six and isn't one of the four products.

explanation: The mixed products are 3-hydroxypentanal (acetaldehyde enolate adding to propanal) and 3-hydroxy-2-methylbutanal (propanal enolate adding to acetaldehyde). The symmetrical products are 3-hydroxybutanal and 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal.

prompt: In a mixture of acetaldehyde and propanal, which aldol product forms when the propanal enolate ion adds to acetaldehyde?

choices.why: That forms when the roles are reversed: the acetaldehyde enolate adds to propanal.
That forms when the propanal enolate adds to a second propanal.
That forms when the acetaldehyde enolate adds to a second acetaldehyde.

explanation: The α carbon of propanal, which carries a methyl group, bonds to the carbonyl carbon of acetaldehyde, and the acetaldehyde oxygen becomes the –OH. The product is 3-hydroxy-2-methylbutanal.

prompt: Which compound can act only as the acceptor in a mixed aldol reaction, making it a good partner for a clean reaction?

choices.why: Acetaldehyde has α hydrogens, so it can form an enolate ion and act as a donor too.
Propanal has α hydrogens; with acetaldehyde it gives a mixture of four products.
Cyclohexanone has α hydrogens and can form an enolate ion, so it can be a donor.

explanation: Benzaldehyde has no α hydrogens, so it can't form an enolate ion to add to another partner, yet it has an unhindered carbonyl group that is a good acceptor of nucleophiles.

prompt: Why is formaldehyde a good partner in a mixed aldol reaction?

choices.text: It can't be a donor (no α hydrogens) but is a good, unhindered acceptor
It is much more acidic than its partner, so it forms its enolate ion first
choices.why: That is the other condition, met by partners such as ethyl acetoacetate. Formaldehyde can't form an enolate ion at all.

choices.text: Its hindered carbonyl group reacts only with strong nucleophiles
choices.why: Formaldehyde's carbonyl group is unhindered, which is what makes it a good acceptor.

choices.text: It forms its enolate ion faster than other aldehydes do
choices.why: Formaldehyde has no α hydrogens, so it can't form an enolate ion.

explanation: A mixed aldol reaction is likely to succeed if one partner has no α hydrogens (so it can't become a donor) but has an unhindered carbonyl group (so it is a good acceptor). Benzaldehyde and formaldehyde both fit.

prompt: What is the product when 2-methylcyclohexanone reacts with benzaldehyde and sodium ethoxide in ethanol?

choices.why: The product has a C=C between the ring and the benzylidene carbon; water is lost, as the section's equation shows.

choices.text: A mixture of four aldol products
choices.why: Benzaldehyde has no α hydrogens, so it can only be the acceptor. The section reports a single mixed product in 78% yield.

choices.text: The aldol product of two benzaldehyde molecules
choices.why: Benzaldehyde can't form an enolate ion, so it can't add to another benzaldehyde.

explanation: Benzaldehyde can only act as the acceptor. The enolate of 2-methylcyclohexanone adds to it, and loss of water gives 2-benzylidene-6-methylcyclohexanone in 78% yield.

prompt: 2-Methylcyclohexanone (C7H12O) and benzaldehyde (C7H6O) give 2-benzylidene-6-methylcyclohexanone and water. How many hydrogen atoms does the product contain?
explanation: C7H12O + C7H6O = C14H18O2. Losing one H2O gives C14H16O, so the product has 18 − 2 = 16 hydrogens.

prompt: Why does ethyl acetoacetate give a single mixed aldol product with a monoketone?

choices.text: It is much more acidic, so it forms its enolate ion in preference
It has no α hydrogens, so it can only act as the acceptor
choices.why: Ethyl acetoacetate has acidic α hydrogens; in this reaction it is the donor.

choices.text: Its unhindered carbonyl group makes it the best acceptor present
choices.why: In these reactions ethyl acetoacetate is the enolate donor and the monoketone is the acceptor.

choices.text: Monoketones can't act as acceptors in aldol reactions at all
choices.why: The monoketone is the acceptor here; cyclohexanone, for example, accepts the ethyl acetoacetate enolate.

explanation: A mixed aldol reaction succeeds if one partner is much more acidic than the other. Ethyl acetoacetate is completely converted into its enolate ion in preference to enolate formation from monocarbonyl partners, so it acts as the donor.

prompt: What is the product of the mixed aldol reaction of cyclohexanone with ethyl acetoacetate and sodium ethoxide?

choices.why: That would need cyclohexanone to be the donor. Ethyl acetoacetate is converted into its enolate ion in preference.
The donor carbon is the acidic CH2 between the two carbonyl groups (carbon 2), not the methyl carbon.
That has no C=C. Water is lost, so the product has a C=C to the cyclohexylidene ring.

explanation: The ethyl acetoacetate enolate adds to cyclohexanone, and loss of water gives ethyl 2-cyclohexylidene-3-oxobutanoate in 80% yield.

prompt: Which compound can probably be prepared cleanly by a mixed aldol reaction (Exercise 23.5.1)?

choices.why: That would need acetophenone and acetone. Both have α hydrogens and neither is unusually acidic, so a mixture would form.
That would need cyclohexanone and propanal, which both have α hydrogens, so a mixture would form.
That is a mixed product of propanal and acetaldehyde, which give a mixture of four products.

explanation: 4-Phenyl-3-buten-2-one comes from C6H5CHO + CH3COCH3. Benzaldehyde has no α hydrogens but is a good acceptor, so acetone is the only possible donor and one product forms.
